        j_S:\B(S)\hookrightarrow \A(S)
\]
be the inclusion.  The associated morphism of topoi is denoted
\[
        \pi_S:\Sh(\A(S))\longrightarrow \Sh(\B(S)).
\]
When \(S=P\) we write simply \(\pi\).

\section{Formal reductions}

\begin{lemma}[Slices]\label{lem:slices}
Let \(b=b_x=P[-x]^\sh\in B_P\).  Then the slice site
\((A_P^{\op})/b\) is canonically equivalent to \(A_b^{\op}\).  Under this
equivalence, \(B_P^{\op}/b\) identifies with \(B_b^{\op}\).  Consequently,
for every sheaf \(G\) on \(A_P^{\op}\),
\[
        (R\pi_\ast G)(b)\simeq
        R\Gamma\bigl(A_b^{\op},\,G|_{A_b^{\op}}\bigr).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
An object of \((A_P^{\op})/b\) is an object \(P\to Q\) of \(A_P\) together
with a morphism \(Q\to b\) in \(A_P^{\op}\), equivalently a morphism
\(b\to Q\) in \(A_P\).  This is precisely an object of \(A_b\).  The same
argument identifies \(B_P/b\) with \(B_b\), because
\[
        b[-\bar y]^\sh \simeq P[-x-y]^\sh
\]
for every image \(\bar y\in b\).  The formula for derived direct image is
the usual description of the stalk over an object of a site as cohomology on
the slice site; see SGA~4, Exp.~V, Prop.~5.1.
\end{proof}

Thus it suffices to prove the following affine acyclicity statement.

\begin{proposition}[Affine acyclicity]\label{prop:affine-acyclicity}
Let \(S\) be any monoid.  For every presheaf of abelian groups
\(F\colon B_S\to \Ab\), viewed as a sheaf on \(B_S^{\op}\) for the trivial
topology, the natural map
\[
        F(S)\longrightarrow
        R\Gamma\bigl(A_S^{\op},\,\pi_S^{-1}F\bigr)
\]
is a quasi-isomorphism.
\end{proposition}

The proof occupies the next two sections.

\section{Birhizomic hypercovers and their carrier functors}

We recall the local form of the birhizomic topology.  For a fine saturated
sharp monoid \(S\), let \(\sigma_S\) be the rational polyhedral cone
\[
        \sigma_S=\Hom(S,\mathbb R_{\ge 0}).
\]
Its faces correspond to objects of \(B_S\): a face \(F\subset S\) gives the
quotient \(S/F\), equivalently some \(S[-x]^\sh\) after choosing \(x\) in the
relative interior of \(F\).  If \(S\) is not finitely generated, all
statements below are understood on finitely generated saturated submonoids;
finite presentation of the maps involved makes this reduction harmless, and
filtered colimits are exact in \(\Ab\).

The following proposition is the monoid-theoretic input.

\begin{proposition}[Local normal form for birhizomic neighbourhoods]
\label{prop:normal-form}
Let \(S\) be a monoid.  There is a cofinal system of hypercovers
\[
        U_\bullet\longrightarrow S
\]
of the final object of the site \(A_S^{\op}\) with the following properties.

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item To \(U_\bullet\) is associated a small category \(I_U\), the category
of non-empty finite intersections of the members of the cover and their
iterated faces.

\item There is a functor
\[
        \rho_U:I_U\longrightarrow B_S,
\]
called the carrier functor.  If \(\alpha\in I_U\), then \(\rho_U(\alpha)\)
is the unique object \(S[-x_\alpha]^\sh\) determined by the face of \(S\)
which is forced to vanish on the corresponding birhizomic neighbourhood.

\item For every presheaf \(F\colon B_S\to \Ab\),
the Cech--Verdier complex of \(\pi_S^{-1}F\) on \(U_\bullet\) is naturally
the Roos complex computing
\[
        R\!\varprojlim_{I_U} F\circ \rho_U .
\]

\item The carrier functor \(\rho_U\) is initial: for every \(b\in B_S\), the
comma category \((\rho_U\downarrow b)\) has contractible nerve.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
We give the standard proof, since this is the only point at which the
definition of ``birhizomic'' is used.

First assume that \(S\) is fine saturated.  A homomorphism
\[
        v:S\longrightarrow V
\]
to a valuative monoid determines a centre face
\[
        F(v)=\{s\in S\mid v(s)=0\}.
\]
After quotienting by \(F(v)\), the non-zero values of \(S/F(v)\) have a
largest archimedean class; this gives a point in the relative interior of a
face of \(\sigma_{S/F(v)}\).  Iterating gives the usual valuative flag of
faces.  The relation \(x\prec y\) records precisely that \(x\) belongs to
the group generated by the face containing \(y\).

Let \(W\) be a rational open star in a sufficiently fine barycentric
subdivision of the conical stratification of \(\sigma_S\).  Choose finitely
many inequalities
\[
        a_i-b_i>0
\]
which cut out \(W\) in the relevant archimedean quotient, and finitely many
elements \(c_j\) whose vanishing cuts out the carrier face.  Define
\(S_W\) to be the sharp saturation of the monoid obtained from \(S\) by

\begin{itemize}
\item forcing the \(c_j\) to become \(0\), and
\item adjoining the differences \(a_i-b_i\).
\end{itemize}

The map \(S\to S_W\) is of finite presentation.  We claim that it is
birhizomic at exactly those valuative points whose visible archimedean point
lies in \(W\).

Indeed, suppose \(S\to M\xrightarrow p N\) is a factorization with
\(p\) infinitesimal, and suppose the valuative point lies in \(W\).  For an
adjoined difference \(a_i-b_i\), its image in \(N\) is positive and is not
infinitesimal relative to the image of \(a_i+b_i\).  In \(M^{\gp}\) one has
\[
        a_i-b_i\prec a_i+b_i,
\]
and in \(N\) one has
\[
        p(a_i+b_i)\prec p(a_i-b_i).
\]
By the defining property of an infinitesimal morphism, \(a_i-b_i\in M\).
Thus all adjoined generators lift.  If \(c_j\) has value \(0\), then both
\(c_j\) and \(-c_j\) are forced in the same way; since \(M\) is sharp this
forces \(c_j=0\).  Hence the factorization through \(N\) lifts uniquely to
\(S_W\).

Conversely, if one of the required strict archimedean inequalities fails,
one constructs an infinitesimal thickening by taking, inside the value
group, the submonoid consisting of all elements whose leading visible value
is positive, together with the image of \(S\).  This submonoid is saturated
and sharp, the map to the given valuative monoid is infinitesimal, but the
failed difference does not belong to it.  Therefore no lift to \(S_W\)
exists.  Similarly, if a forced vanishing condition fails, the corresponding
quotient cannot be lifted.  This proves the claim.

Rational open stars form a basis for the birhizomic topology.  Given any
birhizomic cover, finite presentation shows that only finitely many strict
archimedean inequalities and vanishing conditions occur locally.  Refining
the associated finite conical decomposition by a barycentric subdivision, we
obtain a star cover refining the given cover.  Repeating this in each degree
gives a cofinal system of hypercovers.

For such a star hypercover, intersections of stars are again unions of
stars.  The category \(I_U\) is the category of non-empty finite
intersections.  The value of the left Kan extension of \(F\) on the
corresponding monoid is exactly \(F(\rho_U(\alpha))\); sheafification does
not change these values on the hypercover because the stars are
birhizomic-acyclic by the preceding lifting criterion.  Hence the
Cech--Verdier complex is the Roos complex of \(F\circ \rho_U\).

It remains to check initiality.  Fix \(b=S[-x]^\sh\in B_S\), corresponding
to a face \(\tau\) of the cone.  The comma category
\((\rho_U\downarrow b)\) is the category of stars whose carriers specialize
to \(\tau\).  Geometrically this is the face category of a good star cover
of the closed star of \(\tau\).  That closed star is a convex polyhedral
cone, hence contractible; by the nerve lemma, the nerve of
\((\rho_U\downarrow b)\) is contractible.  Thus \(\rho_U\) is initial.

For a general saturated sharp monoid \(S\), every finite stage of a
finite-presentation hypercover descends to a fine saturated submonoid
\(S_0\subset S\).  The preceding construction applied to \(S_0\), followed
by saturated base change to \(S\), gives the required star hypercovers of
\(S\).  Since the indexing system of such \(S_0\)'s is filtered and filtered
colimits are exact in abelian groups, the same cofinality and acyclicity
statements hold for \(S\).
\end{proof}

We shall also use the following standard cofinality theorem.

\begin{lemma}[Cofinality for derived limits]\label{lem:cofinality}
Let \(u:J\to I\) be an initial functor, meaning that
\((u\downarrow i)\) has contractible nerve for every \(i\in I\).  Then, for
every functor \(E:I\to \Ab\), the natural map
\[
        R\!\varprojlim_I E
        \longrightarrow
        R\!\varprojlim_J E\circ u
\]
is an isomorphism in the derived category.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
This is the derived form of the usual cofinality theorem for limits.  It is
equivalent to Quillen's Theorem~A applied to the Grothendieck construction
of \(E\), or to SGA~4, Exp.~I, Prop.~8.1.3.
\end{proof}

\section{Proof of affine acyclicity}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:affine-acyclicity}]
Let \(F:B_S\to \Ab\) be given.  By Verdier's hypercovering theorem
(SGA~4, Exp.~Vbis, Th.~7.4.1), the cohomology
\[
        R\Gamma(A_S^{\op},\pi_S^{-1}F)
\]
is computed as the filtered colimit over any cofinal system of hypercovers
of the corresponding Cech--Verdier complexes.  We use the cofinal system of
Proposition~\ref{prop:normal-form}.

For a hypercover \(U_\bullet\) in that system, Proposition
\ref{prop:normal-form} identifies the Cech--Verdier complex with
\[
        R\!\varprojlim_{I_U} F\circ \rho_U .
\]
Since \(\rho_U:I_U\to B_S\) is initial, Lemma~\ref{lem:cofinality} gives
\[
        R\!\varprojlim_{I_U} F\circ \rho_U
        \simeq
        R\!\varprojlim_{B_S} F .
\]
But \(B_S\) has an initial object, namely \(S=S[-0]^\sh\).  Therefore the
ordinary limit of \(F\) over \(B_S\) is \(F(S)\), and evaluation at an
initial object is exact.  Hence
\[
        R\!\varprojlim_{B_S}F \simeq F(S)
\]
concentrated in degree \(0\).  Thus every hypercover in the cofinal system
computes the same complex \(F(S)\), and the transition maps are the identity
under this identification.  Consequently
\[
        R\Gamma(A_S^{\op},\pi_S^{-1}F)\simeq F(S).
\]
The identification is the one induced by the adjunction unit, so the map
\(F(S)\to R\Gamma(A_S^{\op},\pi_S^{-1}F)\) is a quasi-isomorphism.
\end{proof}

\section{The global statement}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main}
Let \(P\) be a monoid.  For every presheaf of abelian groups
\(F\) on \(B_P^{\op}\), the adjunction morphism
\[
        F\longrightarrow R\pi_\ast \pi^{-1}F
\]
is a quasi-isomorphism.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Because the topology on \(B_P^{\op}\) is trivial, quasi-isomorphisms of
complexes of sheaves on \(B_P^{\op}\) are detected objectwise.

Fix \(b=P[-x]^\sh\in B_P\).  By Lemma~\ref{lem:slices},
\[
        (R\pi_\ast\pi^{-1}F)(b)
        \simeq
        R\Gamma\bigl(A_b^{\op},
        \pi_b^{-1}(F|_{B_b})\bigr).
\]
Applying Proposition~\ref{prop:affine-acyclicity} to the monoid \(b\), we
obtain
\[
        R\Gamma\bigl(A_b^{\op},
        \pi_b^{-1}(F|_{B_b})\bigr)
        \simeq
        F(b)
\]
concentrated in degree \(0\).  Under this identification, the adjunction
unit
\[
        F(b)\longrightarrow (R\pi_\ast\pi^{-1}F)(b)
\]
is the identity.  Since this holds for every \(b\in B_P\), the morphism
\[
        F\longrightarrow R\pi_\ast\pi^{-1}F
\]
is an objectwise quasi-isomorphism, hence a quasi-isomorphism of sheaves on
\(B_P^{\op}\).
\end{proof}
